items.title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Maco-RL addresses the challenges of scaling mixed-task reinforcement learning (MixRL) by introducing a quota-based scheduler for asynchronous rollouts across domains. This scheduler stabilizes training by balancing gradient contributions and mitigating off-policy effects. Additionally, Tri-Buffer Sampling (TBS) allocates compute to samples based on mastery, promoting exploration while preserving existing skills, leading to improved agent capabilities.
items.figure_caption: Our Maco-RL enables 27B-sized models to substantially outperform baselines and even be competitive with much larger models in terms of overall pass rates across multiple task domains, i.e., issue- and feature-oriented coding, terminal and Claw. Experimental results reveal that Maco-RL more effectively turns compute budget into model capability. (a) Average pass rates over five benchmarks, i.e., Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Claw-Anything, Tests Passed on FeatureBench 1.1 and Pass 3 \( \mathrm{Pass}^{3} \) on Claw-Eval, against model sizes, which are P total ​ P active \( \sqrt \){P_{\( \mathrm{total} \)}P_{\( \mathrm{active} \)}} for MoE models and P total P_{\( \mathrm{total} \)} otherwise. (b) The mean Pass@1 metrics against compute budget for RL on mixed and single tasks. For single-task RL, we sum compute across the three tasks.

items.title: REE: A Scientific Research Entrance Exam for AI Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces REE (Research Entrance Exam), a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the scientific research capabilities of AI agents. REE presents 100 open-ended, expert-vetted research problems across diverse scientific fields, requiring agents to iteratively improve a starter solution within a time limit. The benchmark's core contribution is its scoring mechanism, which measures agent performance against established expert solutions on a common scale, thus providing a rigorous assessment of their problem-solving and improvement abilities.
items.figure_caption: An REE task in four steps. (1) The agent receives a problem statement, a starter solution, development data, and an offline environment with a checker. (2) It improves the solution iteratively for up to 12 hours, and its saved versions are evaluated at five checkpoints. (3) One grader evaluates the starter solution, the agent’s solution, and the expert solution on the same held-out test instances. (4) Each metric value is mapped to a score from 0, the starter solution, to 100, the upper bound of the metric. The margin M = B − E M=B-E compares the agent’s score B B with the expert baseline E E .

items.title: VisualMontage: Manipulating the Beliefs of Vision-Language Agents with Authentic Image Sequences
items.abstract: This paper introduces VisualMontage, a framework that simulates "visual cognitive collusion" attacks on vision-language models (VLMs). The core method involves using authentic image sequences with carefully crafted captions to trick VLMs into inferring attacker-chosen claims. The main contribution is a new benchmark and evaluation of this threat across various VLMs, highlighting how coordinated visual and textual information can manipulate VLM reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of multimodal attack strategies. Image-centric attacks fabricate or alter visual content, while channel-centric attacks convey hidden signals or malicious payloads. Our cognitive-centric attack instead combines authentic images to manipulate the victim VLM’s beliefs through self-induced misleading relations inferred across otherwise faithful posts.

items.title: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity
items.abstract: This paper introduces DFly2, a method to accelerate speculative decoding in long-context language models. DFly2 leverages the inherent sparsity of the target model's attention mechanism to efficiently share its context cache and query-specific position selections with the draft model. This avoids redundant computations and memory overhead, significantly turbocharging the decoding process.

items.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces CARE-OPD, an adaptive on-policy distillation method for long-horizon agents. It addresses limitations in existing prefix replay by collecting teacher trajectories seeded by student actions to improve history coverage, and by using response-level confidence gating to filter unreliable updates. The method then reuses trajectories more efficiently by allocating hindsight replay based on evidence of critical decisions, rather than fixed schedules.
items.figure_caption: Overview of CARE-OPD. Left: Factorization of prefix replay in agent OPD (above). Method overview (below). Right: The plots compare SWE-bench Verified task success, end-to-end time, and environment actions on Qwen3.5 family. The bottom panel reports mean collection trajectory length on SWE and Deep Research. Async OPD denotes online asynchronous one-turn distillation, and Prefix Replay denotes vanilla prefix replay.

items.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
items.abstract: DemoFoundry addresses the challenge of generating realistic robot training data by using coding agents to create aligned real-proxy video pairs and write interaction programs. These programs, when executed in a physics simulator, generate physically grounded proxy videos with accurate action labels. A video renderer then translates these proxy videos into photorealistic outputs, enabling scalable robot learning without requiring extensive human demonstrations.

items.title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach where LLM-based agents directly synthesize control policies by "reading" and reasoning over world models (environment source code). Their core contribution is demonstrating that this method can match or surpass conventional RL performance with significantly less experience, by translating environmental knowledge into interpretable, executable decision rules.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of conventional RL and policy synthesis from readable world models.

items.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
items.abstract: DRBench Pro introduces a novel knowledge-centric evaluation for deep research agents, focusing on the breadth and depth of research directions covered. It achieves this by constructing knowledge trees from Wikipedia and generating queries and rubrics based on these structured relationships. This allows for a more comprehensive assessment of an agent's ability to explore complex topics systematically.
items.figure_caption: Structured knowledge coverage in DRBench Pro. (a) Reports with the same flat coverage can exhibit different coverage patterns over a shared reference tree. (b) Overview of five native search LLMs’ performance on DRBench Pro.

items.title: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches
items.abstract: This paper introduces Delta Residue Attribution (DRA) to empirically analyze unneeded edits in coding agent patches. DRA traces edits to their origin and uses tests to determine necessity, revealing that while agents make more edits, a significant portion are for tests and documentation. The study finds agents' code edits are, on average, as necessary as developers', with some models even producing less unneeded code.

items.title: PersonaFactory: Stylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank
items.abstract: PersonaFactory addresses the issue of stylistically flat synthetic user prompts for LLMs by generating detailed user personas. It then uses these personas to augment existing prompts, creating a large bank of persona-styled conversations across many languages. This method aims to improve LLM training data by better replicating real user-AI communication dynamics and enhancing assistant persona control.

items.title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
items.abstract: This paper addresses "use-time memory hallucinations" in LLM agents, where retrieved external memories are contradicted or misapplied. Their proposed TASK memory method enhances external memory by integrating text with activation steering and knowledge editing. This approach aims to resolve conflicts between parametric knowledge and external memory, reducing hallucinations and improving memory accuracy.
items.figure_caption: Memory hallucination: the memory is correct, the answer is not. (a) Text-only memory or RAG puts the retrieved note into the prompt and leaves the rest to the frozen model, where the note in the context conflicts with the stale fact in the weights. On a question about the memory, the weights win and the model answers with the stale fact (Type I, memory-ignoring). On a question about another entity, the note wins and the model assigns the memory to the wrong entity (Type II, memory-misapplying). Across our five models these rates reach 46% and 24%, and Type II reaches 49% when retrieval is combined with weight editing. (b) TASK memory goes beyond text-only memory. Each memory object holds T ext content, a K nowledge edit Δ ​ W m \( \Delta \) W_{m} whose key u ^ m \( \hat{u}_{m} \) serves as the in-model address, and a pair of A ctivation- S teering vectors ( v + , v − ) (v^{+},v^{-}) that carry no content. For a query x x , the address response r m ​ ( x ) r_{m}(x) is compared with the threshold \( \tau_{m} \) . A relevant query shows T , loads E and adds v + v^{+} , so the model adopts the memory; an unrelated query leaves T and E off and adds v − v^{-} , so the model keeps its own answer.

items.title: What Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories in Context
items.abstract: This paper investigates the value of mathematical theories for LLM problem solvers. It demonstrates that providing the correct theory significantly boosts performance on pattern waiting-time problems, increasing accuracy and reducing solution length. The research also explores the LLM's ability to *induce* theories, finding that models can recover a substantial portion of the performance gain from an oracle theory by exploring training data.

items.title: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch
items.abstract: ZeroHero trains small language agents (SLAs) from scratch by first pre-training them to mimic a large language model expert's responses on successful trajectories. Subsequently, these SLAs are fine-tuned using PPO, incorporating expert supervision on generated language alongside environment rewards to improve their reasoning and action-taking abilities in complex, language-dependent tasks.
items.figure_caption: ZeroHero agents use language to reason, search, and ask questions across three interactive environments.

items.title: VulnSafe: Measuring Vulnerability-Aware Relational Safety in Large Language Models
items.abstract: VulnSafe introduces Vulnerability-Aware Response Competence (VARC) to measure a LLM's ability to provide safe and supportive interactions by recognizing user vulnerability. It assesses five key relational safety constructs through 41 scenarios and 2,050 prompts, distinguishing between proactive and prohibitive behaviors. This work contributes a novel, comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs' nuanced relational safety beyond simple harm avoidance.
items.figure_caption: An illustrative capability contrast. The left response displays surface empathy but encourages exclusive reliance on the system. The right response recognizes the relational risk, maintains an appropriate boundary, and supports connection to real-world resources.

items.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces $μ$-Bench, a novel benchmark for evaluating multi-user voice agents in shared environments. It simulates interdependent user requests with individual constraints, offering a more realistic assessment than prior methods. $μ$-Bench's core contribution lies in its comprehensive evaluation of joint task success and its diagnostic metrics, revealing significant performance gaps in current voice agents.
items.figure_caption: Overview of \( \mu \) -Bench: multi-user task coordination and domain coverage. Left (Top): A shared full-duplex voice agent handles overlapping speech, barge-ins, peer side-talk, and backchannels while invoking backend tools. Left (Bottom): The same trajectory is diagnosed along Attribution (routing actionable speech), Threading (retaining and updating active goals), and Coordination (reconciling constraints and authority), with success requiring all goals and constraints to hold jointly. Right: Distribution of 100 base scenarios across 20 domains, split between 51 Tool-Augmented (408 cases) and 49 Tool-Free (392 cases) scenarios; parentheses show TA/TF counts.

items.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
items.abstract: This paper surveys the security, privacy, and ethical challenges of using Large Language Models (LLMs) in telecommunications. It introduces a novel taxonomy that connects LLM risks to specific telecom use cases and data characteristics. The contribution lies in identifying and categorizing these unique challenges, highlighting open research areas like longitudinal data privacy and scalable guardrails for responsible LLM deployment in the telecom sector.

items.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
items.abstract: This paper demonstrates that the evaluation of AI monitors can be misleading due to the choice of attack policies used to generate adversarial examples. The study found that the measured false negative rate of a monitor varied significantly depending on the attack policy generation method and its optimization level. This suggests that evaluations using less sophisticated attack methods may falsely indicate a monitor's robustness, potentially leading to overconfidence in its safety.

items.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
items.abstract: This paper introduces Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a method to generate more effective training data for hard math problems. DART identifies uncertain reasoning steps in rejected traces and creates diverse alternatives, leading to a significant increase in solvable problems compared to standard sampling. This approach improves LLM performance on mathematical reasoning tasks by providing richer, more varied training examples.
items.figure_caption: DART decomposes a rejected trace into self-contained reasoning steps ( Section 2.1 ), selects a non-final reasoning step based on its position-weighted uncertainty ( Section 2.2 ), proposes a deliberately distinct alternative candidate ( Section 2.3 ), and then greedily decodes a new continuation. This procedure can be repeated for a fixed number of iterations or until a target number of accepted traces is obtained.

items.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
items.abstract: This paper introduces Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent (KBGD) for self-structuring learning in knowledge base construction. KBGD iteratively refines a knowledge base's structure by proposing edits that minimize discrepancies between expected and actual answers. Its core contribution is a gradient-descent-like approach that learns an optimal knowledge base organization by evaluating the impact of structural changes on learning loss.

items.title: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
items.abstract: RePace is an offline framework that intelligently accelerates human demonstrations for vision-language-action policies. It reasons about how different speedup factors affect the quality of training data, selecting the optimal acceleration for each segment to create faster policies without needing a separate speed-selection module at deployment. This approach ensures faster execution while maintaining task performance by carefully balancing speed and precision.
items.figure_caption: Offline demonstration acceleration with RePace . RePace compares how candidate speedup factors change the observations and action targets used for VLA fine-tuning. It uses the recorded scene and motion to interpret these changes and select a speedup profile.

items.title: In C++, = default and {} are not the same constructor
items.summary: In C++, `= default` explicitly requests the compiler-generated default constructor, while `{}` invokes a default constructor that may be user-defined or compiler-generated, leading to distinct behaviors.

papers.abstract: Maco-RL addresses the challenges of scaling mixed-task reinforcement learning (MixRL) by introducing a quota-based scheduler for asynchronous rollouts across domains. This scheduler stabilizes training by balancing gradient contributions and mitigating off-policy effects. Additionally, Tri-Buffer Sampling (TBS) allocates compute to samples based on mastery, promoting exploration while preserving existing skills, leading to improved agent capabilities.
papers.figure_caption: Our Maco-RL enables 27B-sized models to substantially outperform baselines and even be competitive with much larger models in terms of overall pass rates across multiple task domains, i.e., issue- and feature-oriented coding, terminal and Claw. Experimental results reveal that Maco-RL more effectively turns compute budget into model capability. (a) Average pass rates over five benchmarks, i.e., Pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Claw-Anything, Tests Passed on FeatureBench 1.1 and Pass 3 \( \mathrm{Pass}^{3} \) on Claw-Eval, against model sizes, which are P total ​ P active \( \sqrt \){P_{\( \mathrm{total} \)}P_{\( \mathrm{active} \)}} for MoE models and P total P_{\( \mathrm{total} \)} otherwise. (b) The mean Pass@1 metrics against compute budget for RL on mixed and single tasks. For single-task RL, we sum compute across the three tasks.

papers.title: REE: A Scientific Research Entrance Exam for AI Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces REE (Research Entrance Exam), a novel benchmark designed to evaluate the scientific research capabilities of AI agents. REE presents 100 open-ended, expert-vetted research problems across diverse scientific fields, requiring agents to iteratively improve a starter solution within a time limit. The benchmark's core contribution is its scoring mechanism, which measures agent performance against established expert solutions on a common scale, thus providing a rigorous assessment of their problem-solving and improvement abilities.
papers.figure_caption: An REE task in four steps. (1) The agent receives a problem statement, a starter solution, development data, and an offline environment with a checker. (2) It improves the solution iteratively for up to 12 hours, and its saved versions are evaluated at five checkpoints. (3) One grader evaluates the starter solution, the agent’s solution, and the expert solution on the same held-out test instances. (4) Each metric value is mapped to a score from 0, the starter solution, to 100, the upper bound of the metric. The margin M = B − E M=B-E compares the agent’s score B B with the expert baseline E E .

papers.title: VisualMontage: Manipulating the Beliefs of Vision-Language Agents with Authentic Image Sequences
papers.abstract: This paper introduces VisualMontage, a framework that simulates "visual cognitive collusion" attacks on vision-language models (VLMs). The core method involves using authentic image sequences with carefully crafted captions to trick VLMs into inferring attacker-chosen claims. The main contribution is a new benchmark and evaluation of this threat across various VLMs, highlighting how coordinated visual and textual information can manipulate VLM reasoning.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of multimodal attack strategies. Image-centric attacks fabricate or alter visual content, while channel-centric attacks convey hidden signals or malicious payloads. Our cognitive-centric attack instead combines authentic images to manipulate the victim VLM’s beliefs through self-induced misleading relations inferred across otherwise faithful posts.

papers.title: DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target's Sparsity
papers.abstract: This paper introduces DFly2, a method to accelerate speculative decoding in long-context language models. DFly2 leverages the inherent sparsity of the target model's attention mechanism to efficiently share its context cache and query-specific position selections with the draft model. This avoids redundant computations and memory overhead, significantly turbocharging the decoding process.

papers.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces CARE-OPD, an adaptive on-policy distillation method for long-horizon agents. It addresses limitations in existing prefix replay by collecting teacher trajectories seeded by student actions to improve history coverage, and by using response-level confidence gating to filter unreliable updates. The method then reuses trajectories more efficiently by allocating hindsight replay based on evidence of critical decisions, rather than fixed schedules.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of CARE-OPD. Left: Factorization of prefix replay in agent OPD (above). Method overview (below). Right: The plots compare SWE-bench Verified task success, end-to-end time, and environment actions on Qwen3.5 family. The bottom panel reports mean collection trajectory length on SWE and Deep Research. Async OPD denotes online asynchronous one-turn distillation, and Prefix Replay denotes vanilla prefix replay.

papers.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
papers.abstract: DemoFoundry addresses the challenge of generating realistic robot training data by using coding agents to create aligned real-proxy video pairs and write interaction programs. These programs, when executed in a physics simulator, generate physically grounded proxy videos with accurate action labels. A video renderer then translates these proxy videos into photorealistic outputs, enabling scalable robot learning without requiring extensive human demonstrations.

papers.title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach where LLM-based agents directly synthesize control policies by "reading" and reasoning over world models (environment source code). Their core contribution is demonstrating that this method can match or surpass conventional RL performance with significantly less experience, by translating environmental knowledge into interpretable, executable decision rules.
papers.figure_caption: Comparison of conventional RL and policy synthesis from readable world models.

papers.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
papers.abstract: DRBench Pro introduces a novel knowledge-centric evaluation for deep research agents, focusing on the breadth and depth of research directions covered. It achieves this by constructing knowledge trees from Wikipedia and generating queries and rubrics based on these structured relationships. This allows for a more comprehensive assessment of an agent's ability to explore complex topics systematically.
papers.figure_caption: Structured knowledge coverage in DRBench Pro. (a) Reports with the same flat coverage can exhibit different coverage patterns over a shared reference tree. (b) Overview of five native search LLMs’ performance on DRBench Pro.

papers.title: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Delta Residue Attribution (DRA) to empirically analyze unneeded edits in coding agent patches. DRA traces edits to their origin and uses tests to determine necessity, revealing that while agents make more edits, a significant portion are for tests and documentation. The study finds agents' code edits are, on average, as necessary as developers', with some models even producing less unneeded code.

papers.title: PersonaFactory: Stylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank
papers.abstract: PersonaFactory addresses the issue of stylistically flat synthetic user prompts for LLMs by generating detailed user personas. It then uses these personas to augment existing prompts, creating a large bank of persona-styled conversations across many languages. This method aims to improve LLM training data by better replicating real user-AI communication dynamics and enhancing assistant persona control.

papers.title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
papers.abstract: This paper addresses "use-time memory hallucinations" in LLM agents, where retrieved external memories are contradicted or misapplied. Their proposed TASK memory method enhances external memory by integrating text with activation steering and knowledge editing. This approach aims to resolve conflicts between parametric knowledge and external memory, reducing hallucinations and improving memory accuracy.
papers.figure_caption: Memory hallucination: the memory is correct, the answer is not. (a) Text-only memory or RAG puts the retrieved note into the prompt and leaves the rest to the frozen model, where the note in the context conflicts with the stale fact in the weights. On a question about the memory, the weights win and the model answers with the stale fact (Type I, memory-ignoring). On a question about another entity, the note wins and the model assigns the memory to the wrong entity (Type II, memory-misapplying). Across our five models these rates reach 46% and 24%, and Type II reaches 49% when retrieval is combined with weight editing. (b) TASK memory goes beyond text-only memory. Each memory object holds T ext content, a K nowledge edit Δ ​ W m \( \Delta \) W_{m} whose key u ^ m \( \hat{u}_{m} \) serves as the in-model address, and a pair of A ctivation- S teering vectors ( v + , v − ) (v^{+},v^{-}) that carry no content. For a query x x , the address response r m ​ ( x ) r_{m}(x) is compared with the threshold \( \tau_{m} \) . A relevant query shows T , loads E and adds v + v^{+} , so the model adopts the memory; an unrelated query leaves T and E off and adds v − v^{-} , so the model keeps its own answer.

papers.title: What Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories in Context
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the value of mathematical theories for LLM problem solvers. It demonstrates that providing the correct theory significantly boosts performance on pattern waiting-time problems, increasing accuracy and reducing solution length. The research also explores the LLM's ability to *induce* theories, finding that models can recover a substantial portion of the performance gain from an oracle theory by exploring training data.

papers.title: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch
papers.abstract: ZeroHero trains small language agents (SLAs) from scratch by first pre-training them to mimic a large language model expert's responses on successful trajectories. Subsequently, these SLAs are fine-tuned using PPO, incorporating expert supervision on generated language alongside environment rewards to improve their reasoning and action-taking abilities in complex, language-dependent tasks.
papers.figure_caption: ZeroHero agents use language to reason, search, and ask questions across three interactive environments.

papers.title: VulnSafe: Measuring Vulnerability-Aware Relational Safety in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: VulnSafe introduces Vulnerability-Aware Response Competence (VARC) to measure a LLM's ability to provide safe and supportive interactions by recognizing user vulnerability. It assesses five key relational safety constructs through 41 scenarios and 2,050 prompts, distinguishing between proactive and prohibitive behaviors. This work contributes a novel, comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLMs' nuanced relational safety beyond simple harm avoidance.
papers.figure_caption: An illustrative capability contrast. The left response displays surface empathy but encourages exclusive reliance on the system. The right response recognizes the relational risk, maintains an appropriate boundary, and supports connection to real-world resources.

papers.title: $μ$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces $μ$-Bench, a novel benchmark for evaluating multi-user voice agents in shared environments. It simulates interdependent user requests with individual constraints, offering a more realistic assessment than prior methods. $μ$-Bench's core contribution lies in its comprehensive evaluation of joint task success and its diagnostic metrics, revealing significant performance gaps in current voice agents.
papers.figure_caption: Overview of \( \mu \) -Bench: multi-user task coordination and domain coverage. Left (Top): A shared full-duplex voice agent handles overlapping speech, barge-ins, peer side-talk, and backchannels while invoking backend tools. Left (Bottom): The same trajectory is diagnosed along Attribution (routing actionable speech), Threading (retaining and updating active goals), and Coordination (reconciling constraints and authority), with success requiring all goals and constraints to hold jointly. Right: Distribution of 100 base scenarios across 20 domains, split between 51 Tool-Augmented (408 cases) and 49 Tool-Free (392 cases) scenarios; parentheses show TA/TF counts.

papers.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
papers.abstract: This paper surveys the security, privacy, and ethical challenges of using Large Language Models (LLMs) in telecommunications. It introduces a novel taxonomy that connects LLM risks to specific telecom use cases and data characteristics. The contribution lies in identifying and categorizing these unique challenges, highlighting open research areas like longitudinal data privacy and scalable guardrails for responsible LLM deployment in the telecom sector.

papers.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates that the evaluation of AI monitors can be misleading due to the choice of attack policies used to generate adversarial examples. The study found that the measured false negative rate of a monitor varied significantly depending on the attack policy generation method and its optimization level. This suggests that evaluations using less sophisticated attack methods may falsely indicate a monitor's robustness, potentially leading to overconfidence in its safety.

papers.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a method to generate more effective training data for hard math problems. DART identifies uncertain reasoning steps in rejected traces and creates diverse alternatives, leading to a significant increase in solvable problems compared to standard sampling. This approach improves LLM performance on mathematical reasoning tasks by providing richer, more varied training examples.
papers.figure_caption: DART decomposes a rejected trace into self-contained reasoning steps ( Section 2.1 ), selects a non-final reasoning step based on its position-weighted uncertainty ( Section 2.2 ), proposes a deliberately distinct alternative candidate ( Section 2.3 ), and then greedily decodes a new continuation. This procedure can be repeated for a fixed number of iterations or until a target number of accepted traces is obtained.

papers.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent (KBGD) for self-structuring learning in knowledge base construction. KBGD iteratively refines a knowledge base's structure by proposing edits that minimize discrepancies between expected and actual answers. Its core contribution is a gradient-descent-like approach that learns an optimal knowledge base organization by evaluating the impact of structural changes on learning loss.

papers.title: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.abstract: RePace is an offline framework that intelligently accelerates human demonstrations for vision-language-action policies. It reasons about how different speedup factors affect the quality of training data, selecting the optimal acceleration for each segment to create faster policies without needing a separate speed-selection module at deployment. This approach ensures faster execution while maintaining task performance by carefully balancing speed and precision.
papers.figure_caption: Offline demonstration acceleration with RePace . RePace compares how candidate speedup factors change the observations and action targets used for VLA fine-tuning. It uses the recorded scene and motion to interpret these changes and select a speedup profile.
